about: I've seen all of these. This is the order I'd hand someone: Pulp Fiction first because it's the whole idea at full volume, Reservoir Dogs to see where it came from, then the rest in the order he made them.

records.n: Back up a step to the first film: one warehouse, a heist you never see, and the template for everything after.
Three stories told out of order, and every scene is a conversation you want to hear again.
An anthology; his segment closes it and is the best of a weak set.
His most grown-up film. Elmore Leonard, Pam Grier and Robert Forster, and it takes its time.
The kung fu and samurai half: Lady Snowblood, the Shaw Brothers and anime, played loud.
The western half, quieter and talkier, and the payoff for Vol. 1.
He guest-directed one scene for Rodriguez. On the list for the comics.
His half of Grindhouse. A lot of talk, then one of the great car chases, done for real.
History rewritten in chapters. The farmhouse opening is the best scene he has shot.
A spaghetti western moved to the antebellum South, with Corbucci in its blood.
A snowbound stage play with guns, and his bleakest film.

records.t: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
records.n: The gentlest one: a love letter to Los Angeles in 1969 that rewrites the ending.

about: The New York crime films are the spine. The path opens on Goodfellas, goes back to where it started, and ends on the late films where he looks back at all of it.

records.t: Who's That Knocking at My Door
records.n: The student-made first feature. Mean Streets does it better.
A Roger Corman job he took to learn the trade.
Where it starts: Little Italy, Keitel and De Niro, and the rock and roll soundtrack he never dropped.
A warm detour from the crime films; Ellen Burstyn won the Oscar.
His parents at the kitchen table. Short, and a key to everything.
God's lonely man. Schrader's script and De Niro at his most frightening.
A big, bruised musical that mostly didn't work.
The Band's farewell concert. Essential, but it belongs with the music.
The black and white boxing film most critics call his best.
The funny, scary flip side of Taxi Driver: a would-be comic who wants fame at any price.
One terrible night in SoHo. His funniest film, and the most stylized.
A slick sequel to The Hustler.
The first try at the faith film; Silence is the finished thought.
Thirty years of a crew in two and a half hours, narrated like a confession.
A remake played as a thriller for hire. Fun, not essential.
Edith Wharton: violence done with manners. For after the path.
Goodfellas moved to Las Vegas, bigger and colder.
The Dalai Lama, beautifully shot and very quiet.
Taxi Driver in an ambulance, with Nicolas Cage.
A huge, uneven epic held together by Day-Lewis.
Howard Hughes, handsome and conventional.
Dylan from 1961 to 1966. It belongs with the music.
The Boston remake of Infernal Affairs that finally won him the Oscar.
A twisty genre exercise.
A family film about the birth of cinema.
Goodfellas with stockbrokers and no brakes.
The Jesuit film he spent decades trying to make. The faith side, after all the crime.
The old men at the end of the crime films, looking back. The last chapter of Goodfellas.
Dylan's 1975 tour, with invented parts. With the music.
The Osage murders: a crime film about America itself.

about: Everyone has seen some Spielberg. The path is the ones that hold up as filmmaking, from the blockbusters he invented to the serious late work and the film about his own childhood.

records.n: A TV movie about a truck. Jaws in miniature.
The first feature, a chase across Texas.
The first summer blockbuster, and still the best lesson in what not showing the shark does.

records.t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
records.n: The most personal of the early films: a man who can't stop building a mountain out of mashed potatoes.
A loud comedy that famously flopped.
The adventure film done perfectly.
A suburban childhood after a divorce, with a visitor.

records.t: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
records.n: A darker, sillier sequel.
The first serious picture. Walker deserves better.
Young Christian Bale in a Japanese camp. Worth it after the path.

records.t: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
records.n: The fun one, with Sean Connery.
Peter Pan grown up. For kids.
Crichton turned into the purest spectacle he made.
The same year as Jurassic Park, and the turn to history.
Earnest history.
For the Omaha Beach opening, which changed how war is filmed.
Kubrick's project, finished by Spielberg. Strange and worth arguing about.
Philip K. Dick, and his best science fiction since the 70s.
A light, fast con story; the most fun he has had in years.
His darkest film: revenge and what it costs.
Post-9/11 dread as an invasion film.
Day-Lewis and a lot of talking, which is the point.
Solid Cold War craft.
Pop culture as a theme park.
A good remake of a musical.
His own childhood, which explains everything that came before.

about: Puzzles about time and memory, made at blockbuster scale. The path starts at the one where the puzzle and the feeling are the same thing.

records.n: The no-budget first film, already scrambling the order.
A man with no short-term memory, told backwards, so you're as lost as he is.
A good remake of a Norwegian thriller, and the least his own.
The setup for The Dark Knight.
Two magicians and the cost of a trick. The best of the puzzle films.
The superhero film as a crime epic, and Heath Ledger's Joker.
Heists inside dreams inside dreams.
A big, clumsy ending to the trilogy.
Relativity as a father and daughter story.
Three timelines, a week, a day and an hour, cut together into one evacuation.
The puzzle with the feeling taken out. On the list for completeness.
Physics, guilt and a hearing room. Where the whole career was heading.
Homer at IMAX scale. For after the path.

about: Seven features. Slow, but the slowness is the point. The path starts with the two science fiction films and works toward the hardest ones.

records.n: His diploma film, a short.
The first feature, a war film seen through a boy's dreams, and the most conventional.
The epic: medieval Russia and an icon painter who stops painting.
Science fiction as grief: a space station where the dead come back.
His memory film, with no plot to hold on to. Easier after the others.
Three men walk into the Zone toward a room that grants wishes. The one people end up loving.
A Russian poet stuck in Italy, carrying a candle across a drained pool.
The last film, made while he was dying: a man bargains with God to stop a war.

about: I know Dr. Strangelove, so that's the door. After it, the path goes in order, since each film is a different genre taken as far as it goes.

records.n: The first feature, which he tried to bury.
A short noir; The Killing is the real start.
A racetrack heist told out of order, decades before Pulp Fiction.
The First World War and the generals who spend men like money.
A studio epic he took over and later disowned.
Good, but the Nabokov novel is the thing.
One I know: the end of the world as farce.
Evolution, a computer and a monolith. Watch it on the biggest screen you can.
Burgess, ultraviolence and free will.
Thackeray lit by candles. The most beautiful film here.
King turned into a maze.
Boot camp, then Hue. Two films in one.
The last one: a long night in a New York built on a soundstage.

about: Two modes, the screwball comedies and the cold crime films, and the best ones are both at once.

records.n: The first film: Texas noir where nobody knows what anybody else did.
Their most cartoonish comedy.
Hammett gangsters and a hat in the woods.
A writer in a hotel that may be hell.
A Capra pastiche, lovely to look at.
A kidnapping goes wrong in the snow, and it is somehow a comedy.
The Dude. A Chandler plot with a bowling league.
The Odyssey in Depression-era Mississippi, with the music that started a revival.
Black and white Cain noir. Worth it after the path.
A star comedy for hire.
The weakest remake.
McCarthy, played straight and terrifying.
Idiots and spies; fun, slight.
The Book of Job in 1967 Minnesota. Their most personal film.
Closer to the Portis novel than the John Wayne film.
A folk singer going nowhere in 1961, and a cat.
A love letter to the 1950s studio lot.
Six western stories, from silly to grim.
Shakespeare in stark black and white.
A road-trip caper.

about: Rushmore is my favorite and I've seen Bottle Rocket, so the path is really everything after them.

records.n: Where it started, and one I've seen.
My favorite of his, and the one that made me love him.
A family of fallen prodigies. The saddest of the early films.

records.t: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
records.n: Bill Murray as a fading Cousteau, with Bowie sung in Portuguese.
Three brothers on a train in India. Charming, minor.
Roald Dahl in stop motion, where his style fits best.
Two kids run away on a New England island in 1965.
A caper about a vanished Europe. The peak of the later style.
Stop motion again, less warm than Mr. Fox.
A magazine as an anthology film. All style.
A play about a play about the desert and grief.

records.t: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar
records.n: A Dahl short for Netflix.
For after the path.

about: The ensemble films of the 90s, then a hard turn into stranger, bigger American stories. Two Pynchon adaptations, which is part of why he is here.

records.n: A small, good first film.
The porn industry from disco to the 80s, done like Goodfellas.
A dozen lives in the Valley on one day, and frogs.
Adam Sandler in a strange, tender romance. The hinge between the two halves.
Oil, God and Daniel Day-Lewis. The turn to the big American story.
A drifter and a cult leader after the war.
Pynchon's stoner detective novel, as hazy as it should be.
A dressmaker, his muse and a mushroom.
A loose, sunny Valley coda. Watch it whenever.
The second Pynchon, from Vineland.

about: Two careers side by side: the fiction films, many with Klaus Kinski, and the documentaries he narrates himself. The path braids them.

records.n: The first feature.
An uprising in an institution. Hard to watch.
Desert mirages and a creation myth, an essay film.
A deaf-blind woman and her world.
Kinski on a raft going down the Amazon and out of his mind.
A foundling who grew up in a cellar meets society.
Shot with the cast under hypnosis.
Bruno S. goes to Wisconsin. Ends with a dancing chicken.
Murnau remade with Kinski, and rats.
Kinski again, made right after Nosferatu.
A steamship over a mountain, for real.
The last Kinski film.
Kuwait's burning oil fields filmed like another planet.
A pilot who escaped a Laotian prison camp goes back.
Herzog on Kinski, the man he once planned to kill.
The best of the documentaries: a man who lived with bears, and Herzog arguing with him about nature.
Dieter's story again, as a Hollywood film.

records.t: Encounters at the End of the World
records.n: Antarctica and the people who end up there.

records.t: Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans
records.n: Nicolas Cage and iguanas.
The Chauvet cave paintings, in 3D.
A Texas triple murder and the death penalty.

records.t: Lo and Behold, Reveries of the Connected World
records.n: The internet, as Herzog sees it.
A tribute to the volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft.
The brain and consciousness.

about: Small-town America with something rotten underneath, then dreams that don't resolve. Twin Peaks is on the TV list; Fire Walk with Me comes after it.

records.n: The first feature: industrial dread and a baby. Pure Lynch, with nothing to soften it.
His most conventional and moving film.
The studio wreck he disowned. On the list for the book.
A severed ear in a lawn, and the town under the town.
A lovers-on-the-run road movie through The Wizard of Oz.

records.t: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me
records.n: Laura Palmer's last week. Watch it after the show.
A man turns into another man. A rehearsal for Mulholland Drive.
A G-rated film about an old man on a lawnmower, and one of his best.
Hollywood as a dream that curdles. The masterpiece.
Three hours on digital video, as far as he went.

about: Time passing is the subject: one night, one day in Vienna, twelve years of a boy. The path follows the films that are about that.

records.n: Austin, one handoff after another. The start of the indie 90s.
The last day of school in 1976.
One night in Vienna, talking.
A lucid dream full of philosophers, rotoscoped.
One motel room, three actors.
A great studio comedy, not a key to him.
Nine years later, in real time in Paris.
Philip K. Dick and paranoia, rotoscoped again.
Jack Black and a true Texas murder.
Nine more years, in Greece, and the fight.
Twelve years of filming one kid growing up.
Dazed and Confused in college, 1980.
A fake hit man and real identity, played as a comedy.
Lorenz Hart on one bad night. For after the path.
The making of Breathless. For after the path.

about: Deadpan, music everywhere, and outsiders drifting. Tom Waits, Iggy Pop and the White Stripes all turn up.

records.n: The student film.
The breakthrough: three drifters and long black-and-white shots.
Tom Waits, John Lurie and Roberto Benigni break out of a Louisiana jail.
Three stories in one Memphis hotel, with Elvis in the air.
Five taxi rides in five cities on one night, scored by Tom Waits.
Johnny Depp as William Blake in an acid western, with Neil Young's guitar.

records.t: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
records.n: A hit man who lives by the Hagakure, scored by RZA.
Short talks at tables: Waits and Iggy, Jack and Meg White and a Tesla coil.
Bill Murray visits his old girlfriends.
A hit man and nothing happening, on purpose.
Vampires as burned-out musicians in Detroit.
A bus driver who writes poems. The gentlest one.
The Stooges. For the music side.
A zombie comedy that shrugs.
For after the path.

about: The 90s thrillers I grew up on, then the procedurals about obsession. I know The Game.

records.n: The studio fight he disowned.
Rain, sin and a box.
One I know: a rich man's life rewritten by a company he paid.
Palahniuk, and the end of the 90s.
A tight genre exercise.
Obsession with a case that never closes. His best.

records.t: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
records.n: A man aging backwards. Pretty, slow.
Sorkin's Facebook origin story, cold and fast.

records.t: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
records.n: A cold, good thriller.
A marriage as a crime scene. The first after the path.
The writing of Citizen Kane.
A hit man and his routines.

about: The samurai films that Hollywood and Tarantino borrowed from, and the modern dramas that are just as good.

records.n: The first with Mifune.
A cop loses his gun in a heat wave. Early and very good.
One crime, four stories, no answer.
Dostoevsky in snowy Hokkaido, cut down by the studio.
A dying bureaucrat looks for one thing worth doing.
Three and a half hours that feel like one; the template for the team-up movie.
Macbeth in feudal Japan, in fog.
The film Star Wars borrowed from.
Hamlet in corporate Japan.
A ronin plays two gangs against each other. Became A Fistful of Dollars.
The lighter Yojimbo sequel.
A kidnapping, a businessman's choice and a police procedural.
A long, humane doctor film.
A hunter in the Siberian forest; made in the USSR.
The warm-up for Ran.
King Lear in color, the late epic.
Eight dreams, one with Scorsese as Van Gogh.

about: Genre films, a monster movie, a train, a serial killer, that turn out to be about class.

records.n: The first feature, a dark comedy about a dog.
Korea's first serial killer case and the detectives who couldn't solve it.
A monster in the Han River and a family of losers who go after it.
A mother will do anything to clear her son.
Class war on a train circling a frozen earth.
A super-pig and the meat industry.
A poor family moves into a rich one's house, and the floor drops.
A clone who keeps dying. For after the path.

about: Revenge, beautifully shot, then a turn toward love stories that are just as twisted.

records.n: Soldiers from both sides of the DMZ become friends. The breakthrough.
The first of the Vengeance trilogy, and the coldest.
Fifteen years locked in a room, then five days to find out why.
The last of the trilogy, a woman's plan years in the making.

records.t: I'm a Cyborg, But That's OK
records.n: A mental-hospital romance.
A priest becomes a vampire.
His English-language film.
Fingersmith moved to colonial Korea, told three ways.
A detective falls for a suspect. Hitchcock in the mountains.
A laid-off man eliminates the competition. For after the path.

about: The Python animator who made dystopias and fantasies that look like nobody else's. I know 12 Monkeys.

records.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
records.n: Co-directed with Terry Jones. It's on the comedy shelf.
Medieval muck, the first on his own.
A boy and six dwarves fall through holes in history.
Bureaucracy as nightmare and farce.
The third of the imagination trilogy, a famous mess.
Robin Williams and the Holy Grail in Manhattan.
One I know: time travel and a plague, from La Jetée.

records.t: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
records.n: Hunter S. Thompson, as unhinged as the book.
A studio fight.
Hard going.
Heath Ledger's last film.
A smaller Brazil.

records.t: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote
records.n: Finished after decades. Worth it for the story behind it.
